paragraphs.source_en:
Lines 56–112 survive at the Huntington Library as part of Mary S.’s transcript for the printer
(HM 331, The Huntington Library, San Marino, California; see MYRS iii 113–20), so her jnl
entries for 18–19 December, ‘write out Shelley’s Poem . . . Finish Copying his Poem’ (Mary
Jnl i 244–5) probably refer to this poem, or to R&H, or to both, as the volume’s other con-
tents were already in England. The date of the Advertisement was presumably the date of
despatch to Ollier. The poem itself is dated pointedly in the title, ‘October, 1818’.
 The poem celebrates a single ‘island’ of happiness, temporal and geographical, in
a sea of calamity, and if the physical descriptions were from life, the day celebrated can
be identified. Lines 321–6 describe an autumn sunset with an ‘infantine moon’ and the
planet Venus so close to the moon as to seem to minister light to it. There was a new moon
on 30 September, and a striking conjunction of the newborn moon with Venus occurred
